originalGroup.material:
Theatre Prop Flower Story 017

During the school play, Lila had to give a paper flower to the old gardener. The flower was missing from the prop table when her scene began. She could not stop the whole play to look for it. She stepped onto the stage with empty hands and said, "I brought you something that cannot be held: a promise to return in spring." The pupil playing the gardener understood and replied, "Then I will keep a place for you."
The scene continued. Backstage, a helper found the flower under a folded cloth. Lila wanted to blame him, but then remembered she had moved the cloth before the show. After the performance, the group made a simple prop list and checked each object before its scene. Their teacher praised the quick response on stage, while reminding them that a good recovery did not remove the need to prepare.

Roof Garden Noise Note 017

Dear Jun,
Our block has opened a roof garden. Residents can visit from eight in the morning until seven in the evening. The benches are popular after dinner, but the flats below can hear chairs scraping. The garden team has added soft pads to the chair legs and asked visitors to lift chairs rather than drag them. The new sign also says "Quiet time after six." This does not close the garden at six. It asks people to keep voices low for the final hour. I went yesterday and read on a bench. A neighbour wanted music, so he used his own headphones.
See you soon,
Ada

Dear Jun,

Ada

originalGroup.material:
Clockmaker Window Story 017

Every evening, a clockmaker placed a lamp in his shop window before closing. Theo thought it advertised late opening, so one winter evening he knocked after the door had been locked. The clockmaker opened it and smiled. "The lamp is not for customers," he said.
Across the lane, an elderly neighbour walked home from the community hall. The street light at the corner had failed. The lamp showed the narrow step outside her gate. Theo offered to repair every clock in the shop in return for the explanation. The clockmaker laughed and asked instead whether Theo could report the street light to the town office.
A week later, the street light worked again. The shop lamp disappeared from the window. Theo felt a little disappointed; he had liked the warm glow. Then he saw the neighbour cross the lane without slowing to search for the step. He understood that the lamp had been useful because it answered a particular need. It did not have to become a permanent tradition once that need was met.

originalGroup.material:
School Fair Ticket Bundle 017

At the school fair, each game ticket sold separately for two yuan. To speed up sales, volunteers also prepared bundles of five tickets for ten yuan. The price per ticket did not change. One volunteer recorded "20 sales" without saying whether these were single tickets or bundles. The money box held more than forty yuan, which seemed impossible if every sale meant one ticket.
The team checked the remaining bundles and the written cash entries. They reconstructed how many tickets had been sold and added units to the record. For later shifts, the sheet had separate columns for single tickets, bundles and yuan received. The volunteers still counted the cash at each handover; a clearer sheet reduced confusion but did not replace checking the money itself.
